{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Olympia E. Nicodemi''' is a mathematician and [[mathematics education|mathematics educator]] whose research interests range from [[wavelet]]s to the [[history of mathematics]].{{r|galileo}} She was a distinguished teaching professor of mathematics at the [[State University of New York at Geneseo]] until 2020, when she retired.{{r|profile}}

==Career and publications==
Nicodemi did her undergraduate studies at [[New York University]], and completed her Ph.D. at the [[University of Rochester]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|241930}}</ref> She joined the faculty at SUNY Geneseo in 1981.{{r|profile}} She is the author of ''Discrete Mathematics: A Bridge to Computer Science and Advanced Mathematics'' (West Publishing, 1987) and ''An Introduction to Abstract Algebra: With Notes to the Future Teacher'' (with Melissa A. Sutherland and Gary W. Towsley, Pearson, 2007).{{r|colley}}

==Recognition==
Nicodemi was one of the 2004 winners of the [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]], an award given by the [[Mathematical Association of America]] to outstanding mathematics teachers whose effectiveness extends beyond their own campuses. The award particularly cited her role in the growth of the number of mathematics students at her campus, approximately 2/3 of whom were female.{{r|phoenix}}
